## Historical audit — S0179

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/service_incident_01/retired/results/r2/sceneevolve_cli/C1/test/commons_16007442/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to JSONL lines and decoded-observation character ranges in that file.

| Evidence | Observation and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Goal: line 1, [0,9033) | The request was to reconstruct a 512 × 388 indoor photograph as an editable SceneAct/Blender scene, using separate meshes, inferred geometry and a matching camera. Multiple objects, materials, placement and occlusion were **requested**, not observed in a build. The photograph itself is not visible in this audit. |
| Attempt: line 2, [0,2631) | One fresh student CLI session was launched with the staged image, read-only sandbox and interactive tools disabled. It failed with exit code 1 after about 19.7 seconds; zero tool calls were recorded. The actual model and underlying model-turn count are unknown. |
| Interruption: lines 3 [0,549), 4 [0,1613) | A student `model_error` and subsequent `scene_error` report the failed CLI exit, with a pointer to stderr. The stderr contents are not included, so the underlying cause is unknown. The traceback places the interruption at the model request, not at a scene build or render. |

**Changes and validation.** No student program, scene edit, execution, render, visual comparison or successful build appears in the supplied trajectory. Thus there is no evidence to assess actual multiple objects, materials or textures, part connections, object poses, camera alignment, lighting, or rendering defects. These are unknown, not demonstrated failures of the reconstruction algorithm. No autonomous exploration is visible; the session records no tool calls, although unexposed inference cannot be characterized.

**Teacher input.** No teacher message, detection, diagnosis, proposed update or execution is present. Neither teacher availability nor student receipt or adoption is evidenced.

**Outcome and lessons.** This is a **technical interruption**, with reconstruction quality and formal task success unknown—not an independently verified partial reconstruction or an empty patch. Transferably, a failed model invocation and an unread stderr pointer do not establish a geometry or visual-quality problem; inspect the actual error before attributing cause. The task-specific unresolved questions are what the reference depicts, why the CLI exited, and whether any reconstruction would have met the requested visual and geometric constraints.
